newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINLAND'S MERITA PROFIT ALMOST TRIPLES.
newsitem.headline: FINLAND'S MERITA PROFIT ALMOST TRIPLES.

text.p: Merita Oy, Finland's largest banking group, said Wednesday that stronger stock markets and fewer bad debts helped produce a surge in first-half profits, eneabling it to meet its full-year targets by June.

Reporting operating profit after credit losses at 1.81 billion markka ($324.8 million) against 681 million ($122 million) in the year-ago period, Merita said net loan and guarantee losses were slashed to 325 million ($58 million) from 824 million ($148 million).
"We have achieved the target for the full year already in the first half and see a good development in the second half," a Merita spokeswoman said.
Industry analysts had forecast a median around 1.5 billion markka ($269 million).
"The improvement in performance is attributable in part to the continued decline in expenses and loan losses and an increase in net income from operations," Merita said.

"Another contributory factor was a rise in earnings from equity trading, supported by the favorable trend in the stock market." First-half income on securities trading ballooned to 1.35 billion markka ($242 million), up from 552 million ($99 million).
